q: 'Defectives' in a workshop are distinguished from 'spoilage' in that:

options.A: Defectives can never be rectified, whereas spoilage can always be rectified
options.B: Defectives are sold at full price, whereas spoilage is sold at a discount
options.C: There is no difference between the two terms
options.D: Defectives can be rectified and brought up to the required standard by incurring additional expenditure, whereas spoilage cannot be rectified economically and has to be rejected or sold as scrap

e: Defectives can be rectified and brought up to standard by incurring additional expenditure, whereas spoilage cannot be rectified economically and must be rejected or sold as scrap.

q: The boiler shop of a railway workshop is primarily concerned with:

options.B: Fabrication and repair of boilers, tanks and other plate and pressure-vessel work
options.C: Turning of wheel tyres to profile
options.D: Upholstery of coach seats and berths

e: The boiler shop is concerned with fabrication and repair of boilers, tanks and other plate and pressure-vessel work.

q: The fitting shop of a workshop is primarily concerned with:

options.C: Fitting together and assembly of machined components into sub-assemblies and complete units
options.D: Winding of armatures of electric motors

e: The fitting shop fits together and assembles machined components into sub-assemblies and complete units.

q: The workshop at Liluah, near Howrah, is:

options.A: A carriage and wagon workshop of Eastern Railway
options.B: A locomotive manufacturing unit located at Chennai
options.C: A wagon manufacturing shop at Jamalpur
options.D: The coach factory located at Kapurthala

e: The Liluah workshop near Howrah is a carriage and wagon workshop of Eastern Railway.

q: The Marathwada Rail Coach Factory, a production unit manufacturing passenger coaches, is located at:
e: The Marathwada Rail Coach Factory, which manufactures passenger coaches, is located at Latur.

q: The Vande Bharat (Train 18) train sets were designed and are manufactured at:
e: The Vande Bharat (Train 18) train sets were designed and are manufactured at the Integral Coach Factory, Chennai.

q: The 'LHB' design of passenger coaches takes its name from:

options.A: A British coach-building firm of London
options.B: The initials of the first Indian engineer who designed the coach
options.C: Linke-Hofmann-Busch, the German firm from which the coach technology was obtained

e: LHB stands for Linke-Hofmann-Busch, the German firm from which the coach design and technology were obtained.

q: Replacement of machinery and plant in a workshop under the Machinery and Plant (M&P) Programme is generally justified on:

options.A: The age-cum-condition basis, i.e., the age of the machine and its present condition taken together
options.B: Age alone, every machine being replaced at a fixed age in all cases
options.C: Breakdown alone, a machine being replaced only after it has finally broken down
options.D: The recommendation of the machine manufacturer alone

e: Replacement of machinery under the M and P Programme is generally justified on the age-cum-condition basis - the age of the machine and its present condition taken together.

q: Total Productive Maintenance (TPM), as a maintenance concept, is characterised by:

options.A: Maintenance being left entirely to a specialised maintenance gang
options.B: Maintenance being outsourced to outside agencies
options.C: Attention to equipment only after it breaks down
options.D: Involvement of the operators themselves in the routine care and upkeep of the equipment they operate, aiming at zero breakdowns and zero defects

e: Total Productive Maintenance involves the operators themselves in the routine care and upkeep of their equipment, aiming at zero breakdowns and zero defects.

q: Predictive (condition-based) maintenance of workshop machinery differs from time-based preventive maintenance in that it is carried out:

options.A: At fixed calendar intervals, irrespective of the condition of the machine
options.B: When the monitored condition of the machine (such as vibration, temperature or oil analysis) indicates deterioration and the need for attention
options.C: Only after the machine has broken down
options.D: Only during the annual shutdown of the workshop

e: Predictive maintenance is condition-based: it is carried out when monitored parameters such as vibration, temperature or oil analysis indicate deterioration, unlike fixed-interval preventive maintenance.

q: Under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a Works Committee is required to be constituted in an industrial establishment in which the number of workmen employed is:
e: Under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a Works Committee must be constituted in an industrial establishment employing 100 or more workmen.

q: 'Standing Orders' of an industrial establishment, certified under the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946, primarily:

options.A: Define the terms and conditions of employment, such as classification of workmen, working hours, leave, acts of misconduct and the procedure for termination of employment
options.B: Are issued by the trade union of the establishment
options.C: Fix the rates of wages of the workmen
options.D: Lay down the safety rules to be followed in the factory

e: Certified Standing Orders define the terms and conditions of employment - classification of workmen, working hours, leave, misconduct and termination procedure.

q: Under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, the minimum bonus payable to an eligible employee for an accounting year is:

options.A: 5 per cent of the salary or wage earned
options.B: 8.33 per cent of the salary or wage earned
options.C: 10 per cent of the salary or wage earned
options.D: 20 per cent of the salary or wage earned

e: Under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, the minimum bonus payable to an eligible employee is 8.33 per cent of the salary or wage earned during the accounting year.

q: Under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, the mechanism of 'set-on' and 'set-off' is provided in order to:

options.A: Punish employers who delay payment of bonus
options.B: Create a welfare fund for the employees
options.C: Enable the employer to retain the entire surplus of good years
options.D: Smooth out bonus payments over the years, the excess allocable surplus of a year being carried forward ('set-on') and any deficiency being carried forward ('set-off'), for adjustment in the succeeding years

e: Set-on and set-off carry forward the excess or deficiency of allocable surplus to succeeding years, smoothing out bonus payments over good and bad years.

q: Under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, an employee is eligible for bonus if he has worked in the establishment in the accounting year for not less than:
e: An employee is eligible for bonus under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 if he has worked in the establishment for not less than 30 working days in the accounting year.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the total amount of fines that can be imposed on a worker in any one wage period cannot exceed:

options.A: 3 per cent of the wages payable to him for that wage period
options.B: 5 per cent of the wages payable to him for that wage period
options.C: 10 per cent of the wages payable to him for that wage period
options.D: 25 per cent of the wages payable to him for that wage period

e: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, total fines in any one wage period cannot exceed 3 per cent of the wages payable for that wage period.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the total deductions that can ordinarily be made from the wages of a worker in any one wage period cannot exceed:
e: Total deductions from a worker's wages in any one wage period cannot ordinarily exceed 50 per cent of his wages.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, as amended, wages of the workers must be paid:

options.A: Only in current coin, in all cases
options.C: Only by cheque, in all cases
options.D: In current coin or currency notes, or by cheque, or by crediting the wages in the bank account of the worker

e: Wages must be paid in current coin or currency notes, or by cheque, or by crediting the amount in the worker's bank account.

q: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, an employer is liable to pay compensation to a workman for personal injury caused:

options.A: By an accident occurring anywhere and at any time
options.B: Only where the employer is proved to have been negligent
options.C: By an accident arising out of and in the course of his employment
options.D: Only where the injury results in death

e: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, the employer is liable for personal injury caused by an accident arising out of and in the course of the employment; negligence need not be proved.

q: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where a workman dies as a result of an injury, the compensation:

options.A: Cannot be paid by the employer directly to the dependants, but must be deposited with the Commissioner for distribution among them
options.B: Must be paid by the employer directly to the eldest dependant
options.C: Is paid to the trade union of the deceased workman
options.D: Is payable only after the expiry of one year from the death

e: Compensation for a deceased workman cannot be paid directly to the dependants; it must be deposited with the Commissioner, who distributes it among them.

q: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, occupational diseases peculiar to an employment, specified in Schedule III of the Act, are treated as:

options.A: Injury by accident, and compensation is payable for them as for an accident
options.B: Not compensable under the Act in any circumstances
options.C: Compensable only if the disease takes the form of an epidemic
options.D: Compensable only under the Employees' State Insurance scheme

e: Occupational diseases specified in Schedule III of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 are treated as injury by accident, and compensation is payable for them as for an accident.

q: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, an application for compensation should ordinarily be filed before the Commissioner within:

options.A: Six months of the occurrence of the accident
options.B: One year of the occurrence of the accident
options.C: Five years of the occurrence of the accident
options.D: Two years of the occurrence of the accident

e: An application for compensation under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 should ordinarily be filed before the Commissioner within two years of the occurrence of the accident.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, premises are treated as a 'factory' if a manufacturing process is carried on there with the aid of power by:

options.A: 20 or more workers (10 or more where power is not used)
options.B: 5 or more workers (10 or more where power is not used)
options.C: 10 or more workers (20 or more where power is not used)
options.D: 50 or more workers (100 or more where power is not used)

e: Premises are a 'factory' where a manufacturing process is carried on with the aid of power by 10 or more workers (20 or more where power is not used).

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a young person who has completed fifteen years of age but has not completed eighteen years can be employed in a factory only if:

options.A: A certificate of fitness for such work, granted by a certifying surgeon, is in the custody of the manager of the factory
options.B: He produces a letter of consent from his parents
options.C: He is employed only in the night shift
options.D: No condition applies to his employment

e: A young person between fifteen and eighteen years can be employed only if a certificate of fitness granted by a certifying surgeon is in the custody of the factory manager.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a Welfare Officer is required to be appointed in a factory in which the number of workers ordinarily employed is:
e: A Welfare Officer must be appointed in a factory where the number of workers ordinarily employed is 500 or more.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, adequate and suitable shelters or rest rooms and a suitable lunch room are required to be provided in a factory in which the number of workers ordinarily employed is more than:
e: Shelters or rest rooms and a suitable lunch room must be provided where the number of workers ordinarily employed is more than 150.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, every part of the transmission machinery and every dangerous part of other machinery in a factory must be:

options.B: Guarded only during the visit of the Inspector
options.C: Securely fenced, unless it is in such a position or of such construction as to be as safe as if it were securely fenced
options.D: Kept locked during the night shift only

e: Every dangerous part of machinery must be securely fenced, unless its position or construction makes it as safe as if it were securely fenced.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, leave with wages is admissible to a child worker in a factory at the rate of one day for every:

options.A: 15 days of work performed by him
options.B: 20 days of work performed by him
options.C: 12 days of work performed by him
options.D: 25 days of work performed by him

e: Leave with wages is admissible to a child worker at the rate of one day for every 15 days of work performed by him.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, where a worker is granted leave with wages for a period of not less than four days, the wages for the leave period are required to be paid:

options.A: Only after the worker returns from leave
options.B: To him in advance, before his leave begins
options.C: Along with the wages of the succeeding month in all cases
options.D: Only if the leave exceeds fifteen days

e: Where leave with wages of not less than four days is granted, the wages for the leave period must be paid in advance, before the leave begins.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, employment in any part of a factory for pressing cotton in which a cotton-opener is at work is prohibited in the case of:

options.B: Workers above the age of fifty years
options.C: Workers who have not completed one year of service

e: Employment in cotton pressing where a cotton-opener is at work is prohibited in the case of women and young persons.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, where the State Government declares a manufacturing process or operation to be dangerous, it may make special rules which may provide, among other things, for:

options.A: Increasing the working hours of the workers engaged in the process
options.B: Exempting the factory from all the provisions of the Act
options.C: Periodical medical examination of the workers engaged in the process and prohibition of employment of women and young persons in it
options.D: Transfer of the factory to another State

e: For a process declared dangerous, the State Government may make rules providing for periodical medical examination of the workers and prohibition of employment of women and young persons in it.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, the manager of a factory is required to send a notice of an accident in the factory to the prescribed authorities where the accident causes death, or bodily injury by reason of which the injured person is prevented from working for a period of:

options.A: 48 hours or more immediately following the accident
options.B: 12 hours or more immediately following the accident
options.C: One week or more immediately following the accident
options.D: Any period, however small, in all cases

e: Notice of an accident must be sent where it causes death, or bodily injury preventing the injured person from working for 48 hours or more immediately following the accident.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a woman worker in a factory can ordinarily be employed only between the hours of:

options.D: There is no restriction on her hours of work

e: A woman worker in a factory can ordinarily be employed only between the hours of 6 a.m. and 7 p.m.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, 'overlapping shifts' in a factory are dealt with as under:

options.A: They are permitted without any restriction
options.B: They are permitted with the oral permission of the Inspector
options.C: They are compulsory in continuous-process factories
options.D: They are prohibited — work shall not be carried on by means of a system of shifts so arranged that more than one relay of workers is engaged in the same kind of work at the same time

e: Overlapping shifts are prohibited: work must not be arranged so that more than one relay of workers is engaged in the same kind of work at the same time.

q: The Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 applies, in the first instance, to factories and other establishments employing:
e: The Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 applies, in the first instance, to factories and establishments employing 20 or more persons.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation COFMOW stands for:

options.A: Central Organisation for Modernisation of Workshops
options.B: Central Office for Manufacture of Wagons
options.D: Central Organisation for Maintenance of Workshops

e: COFMOW stands for Central Organisation for Modernisation of Workshops.

q: The Central Organisation for Modernisation of Workshops (COFMOW) is primarily engaged in:

options.B: Centralised procurement of machinery and plant for workshops and production units

e: COFMOW is primarily engaged in the centralised procurement of machinery and plant for workshops and production units of Indian Railways.

q: In the railway classification of Plan Heads, the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is operated under:
e: In the Plan Head classification, Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is operated under Plan Head 72 - Manufacturing Suspense.

q: During Periodic Overhaul in a workshop, the axles of rolling stock are subjected to ultrasonic testing primarily in order to:

options.A: Measure the diameter of the axle journal
options.B: Check the profile of the wheel tyre
options.C: Determine the age of the axle
options.D: Detect internal cracks and flaws not visible on the surface

e: Axles are subjected to ultrasonic testing during overhaul to detect internal cracks and flaws that are not visible on the surface.

q: Night shift (night duty) allowance paid to workshop staff, which cannot be identified with individual jobs, is treated in workshop costing as:

options.A: A direct charge on the jobs worked during the night shift
options.D: A recovery from the staff concerned

e: Night shift allowance cannot be identified with individual jobs, so it is treated as part of on-cost (overhead) in workshop costing.

q: The expenditure incurred by a workshop in recruiting and training fresh workers engaged in place of those who have left is, in cost accounting, treated as:

options.A: A direct labour cost of jobs
options.B: A direct material cost of jobs
options.C: Overhead (on-cost), as it cannot be charged to any particular job

e: Recruitment and training cost of fresh workers cannot be charged to any particular job, so it is treated as overhead (on-cost).

q: During a year, 60 workers who left a workshop were replaced by fresh recruits. The average number of workers on the rolls during the year was 1,200. The labour turnover rate (replacement method) is:
e: Labour turnover (replacement method) = workers replaced / average workers on rolls x 100 = 60 / 1,200 x 100 = 5 per cent.

q: On a workshop job, direct material of Rs 85,000, direct labour of Rs 45,000 and direct expenses of Rs 10,000 are booked. The prime cost of the job is:
e: Prime cost = direct material + direct labour + direct expenses = 85,000 + 45,000 + 10,000 = Rs 1,40,000.

q: Material of Rs 1,20,000 was issued to a workshop job. Material worth Rs 15,000 was returned to stores as surplus and scrap arising on the job was credited for Rs 8,000. The net material cost charged to the job is:
e: Net material cost = 1,20,000 - 15,000 (surplus returned to stores) - 8,000 (scrap credited) = Rs 97,000.

q: A workshop worker whose hourly rate of wages is Rs 60 works 10 hours of overtime, paid at double the ordinary rate. The total wages payable to him for the overtime hours are:
e: Overtime wages = 10 hours x Rs 60 x 2 (double rate) = Rs 1,200.

q: A worker is paid at a piece rate of Rs 12 per unit. If he produces 320 units in a period, his wages for the period are:
e: Piece wages = units produced x piece rate = 320 x Rs 12 = Rs 3,840.

q: The total cost of a shop for a period is Rs 4,50,000 and the standard hours of work produced in the period are 15,000. The cost per standard hour is:
e: Cost per standard hour = Rs 4,50,000 / 15,000 standard hours = Rs 30.

q: A workshop employee, whose last drawn monthly wages were Rs 26,000, retires after completing 20 years of service. His gratuity, at 15 days' wages for every completed year of service (15/26 of the monthly wages for each year), is:
e: Gratuity per year = 15/26 x Rs 26,000 = Rs 15,000; for 20 years = 15,000 x 20 = Rs 3,00,000.

q: A batch of 1,000 standard components is manufactured in a workshop at a total cost of Rs 2,50,000. The cost per component is:
e: Cost per component = Rs 2,50,000 / 1,000 components = Rs 250.

q: The monthly wage ceiling for mandatory coverage of an employee under the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme is:
e: Update: the EPF wage ceiling has since been raised to Rs 25,000 per month. (Source: Gazette Notification S.O. 5109(E) dated 17.09.2026 under Section 2(89), Code on Social Security, 2020, Ministry of Labour & Employment.)

q: The maximum amount of gratuity payable to an employee under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 is:
e: The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 caps the gratuity payable to an employee at Rs 20 lakh, and no gratuity beyond this ceiling is payable under the Act.

q: Under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, the maximum bonus payable to an eligible employee for an accounting year is:

options.A: 8.33 per cent of the salary or wages
options.B: 20 per cent of the salary or wages
options.C: 25 per cent of the salary or wages
options.D: 33.33 per cent of the salary or wages

e: Under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, the bonus payable ranges from the minimum of 8.33 per cent to a maximum of 20 per cent of the salary or wages earned.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, the occupier of a factory shall send a written notice to the Chief Inspector at least ___ before he begins to occupy or use any premises as a factory:
e: The occupier must give written notice to the Chief Inspector at least 15 days before he begins to occupy or use any premises as a factory.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, where the number of workers ordinarily employed in a factory exceeds ___, effective arrangements are required to be made for providing a sufficient supply of cool drinking water during hot weather:
e: Where more than 250 workers are ordinarily employed, effective arrangements for a sufficient supply of cool drinking water during hot weather are compulsory.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, where a worker is deprived of his weekly holiday on account of an exemption order, he is entitled to:

options.A: Payment at double rate in lieu of the holiday
options.B: An additional day of leave with wages
options.C: A holiday in the next calendar year
options.D: Compensatory holidays of an equal number, within the month or within the two months immediately following

e: A worker who loses his weekly holiday because of an exemption order must be given compensatory holidays of an equal number within that month or the two months immediately following.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, the wages payable to a worker for his leave period are calculated at a rate equal to:

options.A: Half of his average monthly earnings
options.B: The daily average of his total full-time earnings for the days on which he actually worked during the month immediately preceding his leave
options.C: The minimum wages fixed for his occupation
options.D: His earnings of the month in which the leave is taken

e: Leave wages are paid at a rate equal to the daily average of the worker's total full-time earnings for the days on which he actually worked during the month immediately preceding his leave.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, the industries involving 'hazardous processes' are specified in:
e: The industries involving hazardous processes are listed in the First Schedule to the Factories Act, 1948.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, the restriction on double employment provides that:

options.A: No adult worker shall be required or allowed to work in any factory on any day on which he has already been working in any other factory, save in prescribed circumstances
options.B: A worker may work in two factories on the same day without any restriction
options.C: A worker cannot be employed in the same factory in two consecutive shifts
options.D: Overtime work in a factory is prohibited altogether

e: Double employment is barred: an adult worker shall not be required or allowed to work in any factory on a day on which he has already been working in another factory, save in prescribed circumstances.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the fines realised from workers in a factory can be utilised:

options.A: For meeting the contingent expenses of the factory
options.B: As a contribution to the Railway's earnings
options.C: For payment of bonus to supervisory staff
options.D: Only for such purposes beneficial to the persons employed in the factory as are approved by the prescribed authority

e: Fines realised from workers can be applied only to such purposes beneficial to the persons employed in the factory as are approved by the prescribed authority; they are not the employer's income.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, before making a deduction from a worker's wages on account of damage to or loss of goods expressly entrusted to his custody, it is necessary that:

options.A: The sanction of the Labour Commissioner is obtained
options.B: The worker is placed under suspension
options.C: The worker is given an opportunity of showing cause against the deduction
options.D: The approval of the recognised trade union is taken

e: A deduction for damage to or loss of goods expressly entrusted to a worker can be made only after giving him an opportunity of showing cause against the deduction.

q: The cost of running the Basic Training Centre (training school) attached to a workshop, where apprentices and staff are trained, is treated in workshop costing as:

options.A: A direct charge on manufacture jobs

e: The Basic Training Centre serves the workshop as a whole and its cost cannot be charged directly to any job, so it is treated as general on-cost of the workshop.

q: The cost of packing and despatching articles manufactured in a workshop for another railway is:

options.A: Charged to the work order (job) concerned
options.B: Borne as general on-cost of the workshop
options.D: Written off as a loss of the workshop

e: Packing and despatching charges relate to the specific outturn manufactured for the other railway, so they are charged to the work order (job) concerned.

q: The stipend paid to trade apprentices undergoing training in a railway workshop is treated in workshop costing as:

options.A: Direct wages of the jobs on which they practise
options.B: A loan recoverable from the apprentices
options.C: Part of the material cost of jobs
options.D: On-cost, since the apprentices are trainees and their stipend is not booked to individual jobs

e: Apprentices are trainees and do not work on individual jobs, so their stipend is not booked to jobs and is treated as on-cost.

q: The cost of working a crane which serves exclusively one shop of a workshop is charged to:

options.A: The general on-cost of the whole workshop
options.B: The jobs on which the crane happens to lift material
options.C: The shop on-cost of the shop served
options.D: The capital account of the workshop

e: A crane serving exclusively one shop is a cost of that shop alone, so its cost is charged to the shop on-cost of the shop served, not spread over the whole workshop.

q: Small hand tools of a consumable nature issued to shops are treated in workshop costing as:

options.B: Consumable stores, their cost being charged to shop on-cost
options.C: Charged in full to the first job on which they are used
options.D: Recovered from the workers using them

e: Small consumable hand tools cannot be traced to individual jobs; they are treated as consumable stores and their cost is charged to shop on-cost.

q: The cost of maintaining the ambulance room and other medical facilities provided for workshop staff is treated in workshop costing as:

options.D: Deducted from the wages of workers

e: The ambulance room and other medical facilities are staff welfare amenities benefiting the whole workshop, so their cost is treated as general on-cost (welfare overhead).

q: Where overtime is worked in a workshop specifically on a job in order to meet an urgent requirement of the customer (indentor), the overtime premium is:

options.A: Charged to shop on-cost in all cases
options.B: Recovered from the workers who worked overtime
options.C: Ignored in the costing of the job

e: Where overtime is worked specifically on a job to meet an urgent requirement of the indentor, the overtime premium is charged to that job itself.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948, the employer's contribution (3.25 per cent of wages) is higher than the employee's contribution (0.75 per cent of wages).
2. Under the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, the employee contributes 12 per cent of his wages and the employer contributes an equal amount.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: under ESI the employer's contribution of 3.25 per cent of wages is higher than the employee's 0.75 per cent, and under the EPF Scheme the employee and the employer each contribute 12 per cent.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Cash discount received from suppliers on purchases is a financial receipt and is not deducted from the cost of material in the cost accounts.
2. Interest on capital employed is invariably included as an element of cost in compiling the cost of workshop jobs.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct: cash discount is a financial receipt and is not deducted from the cost of material. Statement 2 is wrong, as interest on capital is not invariably included as an element of cost.

q: The Matunga workshop of Central Railway at Mumbai is primarily engaged in:

options.A: Periodic Overhaul of passenger coaches and EMU stock

e: The Matunga workshop of Central Railway at Mumbai is primarily engaged in periodic overhaul of passenger coaches and EMU stock.

q: The Jamalpur workshop of Indian Railways is well known for the manufacture of:
e: The Jamalpur workshop of Indian Railways is well known for the manufacture of heavy-duty diesel breakdown cranes.

q: The Diesel Loco Modernisation Works at Patiala was originally set up under the name:
e: The Diesel Loco Modernisation Works at Patiala was originally set up under the name Diesel Component Works.

q: The Rail Wheel Factory at Yelahanka (Bengaluru) was originally known as:
e: The Rail Wheel Factory at Yelahanka (Bengaluru) was originally known as the Wheel and Axle Plant.

q: The Carriage Works and the Loco Works of Southern Railway are located at:
e: The Carriage Works and the Loco Works of Southern Railway are both located at Perambur, Chennai.

q: The primary objective of a good plant layout of the machines and equipment in a workshop is to:

options.A: Increase the number of machines installed in the shop
options.B: Reduce the number of workers required in the shop
options.C: Improve the appearance of the shop floor
options.D: Minimise material handling and ensure a smooth flow of work

e: A good plant layout aims at minimising material handling and ensuring a smooth flow of work through the workshop, not merely at fitting in more machines or workers.

q: In a production line in a workshop, the effective output of the line as a whole is determined by:

options.A: The fastest operation in the line
options.B: The bottleneck operation, i.e., the operation with the least capacity
options.C: The first operation in the line
options.D: The average capacity of all the operations

e: The effective output of a production line is determined by its bottleneck operation, the operation with the least capacity, since no other operation can push output beyond it.

q: Annealing of a steel component differs from normalising in that, in annealing, the heated component is:

options.B: Cooled in a blast of air
options.C: Cooled very slowly, generally in the furnace itself, making the steel softer and more ductile
options.D: Heated only up to a low temperature

e: In annealing the heated component is cooled very slowly, generally in the furnace itself, making the steel softer and more ductile; normalising, by contrast, uses air cooling.

q: The bogies used under LHB-design passenger coaches in Indian Railways are of:
e: The bogies used under LHB-design passenger coaches in Indian Railways are of FIAT design.

q: The body shells of LHB-design passenger coaches are made of:
e: The body shells of LHB-design passenger coaches are made of stainless steel, unlike the corten steel shells of conventional coaches.

q: Limit (GO and NO-GO) gauges are used in a workshop for:

options.A: Measuring the exact dimension of a component
options.B: Checking quickly whether the dimensions of a component lie within the prescribed tolerance limits
options.C: Marking out work on a job

e: Limit (GO and NO-GO) gauges do not measure the exact dimension; they quickly check whether the dimensions of a component lie within the prescribed tolerance limits.

q: The opening balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense of a workshop is Rs 8,00,000. During the year, labour, material and on-cost of Rs 35,00,000 are booked to jobs, and outturn of Rs 38,00,000 is transferred out. The closing balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is:
e: Closing balance = opening balance + cost booked to jobs - outturn transferred out = 8,00,000 + 35,00,000 - 38,00,000 = Rs 5,00,000.

q: The total machine expenses of a machine shop for a period are Rs 4,80,000 and the effective machine hours worked in the period are 12,000. The machine-hour rate of the shop is:
e: Machine-hour rate = total machine expenses / effective machine hours = 4,80,000 / 12,000 = Rs 40 per machine hour.

q: The shop on-cost of a shop for a period is Rs 1,50,000 and the direct wages booked to jobs in the shop during the same period are Rs 6,00,000. The shop on-cost rate, as a percentage of direct wages, is:
e: Shop on-cost rate = 1,50,000 / 6,00,000 x 100 = 25 per cent of direct wages.

q: The allowed time for a job is 36 hours and a worker completes it in 24 hours. The efficiency of the worker for the job is:
e: Efficiency = allowed time / time taken x 100 = 36 / 24 x 100 = 150 per cent.

q: The allowed time for a job is 30 hours and a worker completes it in 24 hours. His hourly rate of wages is Rs 50. Under the Halsey premium bonus plan (bonus at 50 per cent of the time saved), the bonus payable to him for the job is:
e: Time saved = 30 - 24 = 6 hours; Halsey bonus = 50 per cent of the value of time saved = 0.5 x 6 x 50 = Rs 150.

q: The allowed time for a job is 30 hours and a worker completes it in 25 hours. His hourly rate of wages is Rs 60. Under the Rowan premium bonus plan, his total earnings for the job (wages for time taken plus bonus) are:
e: Rowan plan: time wages = 25 x 60 = Rs 1,500; bonus = (time saved / allowed time) x time wages = (5 / 30) x 1,500 = Rs 250; total earnings = Rs 1,750.

q: The total cost of Periodic Overhaul of 25 coaches in a workshop during a period is Rs 4,50,00,000. The average cost of Periodic Overhaul per coach is:
e: Average cost of periodic overhaul per coach = 4,50,00,000 / 25 = Rs 18,00,000.

q: In a workshop foundry, 400 tonnes of metal were melted and charged into the cupola during a period, and the weight of good castings produced was 340 tonnes. The yield of the foundry for the period is:
e: Foundry yield = weight of good castings / metal charged x 100 = 340 / 400 x 100 = 85 per cent.

q: A workshop employee, whose last drawn monthly wages were Rs 31,200, retires after completing 25 years of service. His gratuity, at 15 days' wages for every completed year of service (15/26 of the monthly wages for each year), is:
e: Gratuity = 15/26 x monthly wages x completed years of service = (15/26) x 31,200 x 25 = Rs 4,50,000.

q: On-cost absorbed (recovered) on jobs during a period at the predetermined rate is Rs 72,000, while the actual on-cost incurred in the period is Rs 66,000. The position in respect of absorption of on-cost is:
e: On-cost absorbed (Rs 72,000) exceeds the actual on-cost incurred (Rs 66,000), so on-cost is over-absorbed by Rs 6,000.

q: The total cost of a shop for a period is Rs 7,20,000 and the standard hours of work produced in the period are 18,000. The cost per standard hour is:
e: Cost per standard hour = total cost of the shop / standard hours produced = 7,20,000 / 18,000 = Rs 40.

q: Case hardening of a steel component differs from through hardening in that, in case hardening:

options.A: Only the outer surface (case) is hardened, the core remaining comparatively soft and tough
options.B: The whole section of the component is hardened uniformly throughout
options.C: The component is softened all over so that it can be machined easily
options.D: The component is given a protective coating of zinc

e: In case hardening only the outer surface (case) of the component is hardened, while the core remains comparatively soft and tough.

q: Tempering is carried out on a steel component immediately after hardening primarily in order to:

options.A: Increase the hardness of the component still further
options.B: Remove the scale formed on the surface during hardening
options.D: Reduce the brittleness and internal stresses produced by hardening, while retaining most of the hardness

e: Tempering is done immediately after hardening to reduce the brittleness and internal stresses produced by hardening, while retaining most of the hardness obtained.

q: Galvanising is the process of coating iron or steel articles with a layer of:
e: Galvanising is the process of coating iron or steel articles with a protective layer of zinc.

q: In oxy-acetylene (gas) welding, the welding flame is produced by burning:
e: In oxy-acetylene (gas) welding, the welding flame is produced by burning acetylene in oxygen.

q: Which of the following machines produces flat surfaces by means of a reciprocating single-point cutting tool moving over a stationary workpiece?
e: A shaping machine produces flat surfaces by means of a reciprocating single-point cutting tool moving over a stationary workpiece.

q: Grinding is employed on a machined component primarily in order to:

options.A: Remove a large amount of metal quickly
options.B: Obtain very close dimensional tolerances and a fine surface finish by the action of an abrasive wheel
options.C: Cut internal threads in the component
options.D: Join two pieces of metal together

e: Grinding is a finishing process: it obtains very close dimensional tolerances and a fine surface finish by the action of an abrasive wheel, rather than removing metal rapidly.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A jig not only holds and locates the workpiece but also guides the cutting tool during the operation.
2. A fixture only holds and positions the workpiece and does not guide the cutting tool.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: a jig holds and locates the workpiece and also guides the cutting tool, whereas a fixture only holds and positions the workpiece and does not guide the tool.

q: Interchangeable manufacture of components in a workshop means that:

options.A: Every component is finished by hand filing at the time of assembly
options.B: Components are manufactured in one specified workshop only
options.C: A component can be used only in the particular machine for which it was specially made
options.D: Any component made within the specified limits of size will fit and function in any corresponding assembly without further fitting

e: Interchangeable manufacture means any component made within the specified limits of size will fit and function in any corresponding assembly without further fitting.

q: Blow holes in a casting are caused mainly by:

options.A: Gases and moisture entrapped in the mould during pouring of the molten metal
options.B: Excess of flux added to the charge in the cupola
options.C: Too high a proportion of coke in the charge
options.D: Use of metal patterns in place of wooden patterns

e: Blow holes in a casting are caused mainly by gases and moisture entrapped in the mould during pouring of the molten metal.
